segments.content:
Chapter 5: Memory Bread in Exchange for a Breakfast

Li Hongmei didn't even notice it herself, but she was smiling the entire bike ride to work. Everything seemed pleasant to her, and even the sunlight felt much brighter than usual. When she got to her workplace, a colleague in her forties took one look at her and let out a "yo."

"Hongmei, any happy news at home?"

"What happy news? What kind of happy news could someone my age have." Although Li Hongmei said this, she stopped in her tracks and paused the conversation.

This was her waiting for the other person to feed her the line, one of the strange rules of adult conversation.

The loud-voiced woman played along. "Then what is it? Look at you, glowing with happiness. You look a dozen years younger."

At 8:52, almost everyone had arrived at the office. Those dragging their chairs, making tea, flipping through notebooks, and even the person who had taken out their calligraphy practice sheets all perked up their ears.

"Oh, it's nothing, just that my boy earned a bit of money during the summer break." Li Hongmei waved her hand. "He was worried I'd be tired and insisted on not letting me make breakfast this morning."

"Spending that unnecessary money to buy breakfast, and he even said he'd take care of all the breakfasts from now on."

Having reached middle age, besides gossiping amongst themselves, the only pleasure for this group of women in the system was complaining about their husbands and showing off their children, which brought a glow to their faces.

"Your son has become so sensible, how rare. My little brat only knows how to play games." The loud-voiced woman chimed in, and a single stone set off a thousand ripples.

The older colleagues around them echoed her sentiment a few times. The younger ones couldn't get a word in, but a newcomer chimed in with a bright smile.

"Auntie Li, how are your son's grades?"

Some people truly possessed an extraordinary talent for making a topic awkward with just one sentence. Everyone in the office knew that Li Hongmei's son had average grades and that getting into a university would be a stretch.

Knock, knock, knock!

The sound of knocking came from the door. Xu Qianqian pulled the door open a crack, annoyed. As expected, it was Jiang Nian.

"What are you doing so early in the morning, are you crazy!"

With a rustle, a breakfast was presented to her. Xu Qianqian froze for a second, a little taken aback.

"D-don't you try to bribe me!"

"Just eat it since I'm giving it to you, quit your jabbering," Jiang Nian said with a click of his tongue.

The summer days were especially hard to endure. A single breakfast broke the barrier between the two. Xu Qianqian didn't say it, but she was still a little moved, especially since she was hungry.

"Thanks."

"No need. Let me copy your homework after you're done."

Xu Qianqian: "..."

The dining table was split in two. Xu Qianqian was on one side, eating her breakfast with small, slow bites, while Jiang Nian was on the other, furiously copying homework. They weren't in the same class, but their science worksheets were the same.

He didn't dare to copy everything, only the answers that were within his own level.

With nothing else to do, Xu Qianqian squinted her eyes, watching the molten gold sunlight stream through the window, then glanced at Jiang Nian, who was hard at work at the table.

"Hey, have you ever thought about improving your grades?"

Hearing this, Jiang Nian's pen paused, and he looked up with a frown.

"I have, it's just that I have two lines of thought in my head. One is empty, and the other is also empty."

Xu Qianqian was speechless. "Then what are you going to do about the gaokao?"

Jiang Nian sighed. "I want to study too, but there's so much homework in the third year. My foundation is already weak, and all my time is spent on doing homework."

"That's because you're slow."

"I'm slow because I don't know how to do it." He spread his hands. "After finishing this one, I'm already out of time for the next subject. What can I do but copy?"

Xu Qianqian crossed her arms. "Tch, that's clearly just an excuse."

Ding!

[Learning quest triggered: Live and learn.

At thirty-eight, you are newly divorced and standing at a crossroads in life. In your forties, turning your life around requires not only a strong body but also the cultivation of an appreciation for beauty.

Quest: Have a pleasant conversation with Xu Qianqian. Reward: Memory Bread (five hours). In this state, you can quickly memorize knowledge.]

Jiang Nian stared at the panel, a little dumbfounded. What kind of bull quest progress was the system issuing? So... his future self was pursuing Xu Qianqian?

It wasn't that he was against it, he just found the feeling a bit strange.

Whatever, the reward was what mattered.

"Xu Qianqian, you're right!" Jiang Nian suddenly grew serious, looking at the girl across the table with a solemn expression. "Giving up is easy, but persevering is hard."

"My English is bad. On account of me buying you breakfast, can you teach me how to memorize vocabulary?"

It wasn't that he had truly become motivated; he just knew very well that Xu Qianqian's English was excellent. She was the English class representative and got a perfect score on almost every test.

What was even more insane was that not only had she memorized all 3,500 words for the gaokao, but she had also memorized the vocab for CET-4 and CET-6 along the way. As long as someone asked about English, she would be very happy.

Sure enough, Jiang Nian's words had scratched her right where she itched. Her eyes curved into crescents.

"Alright, for the sake of breakfast... this princess will graciously tell you."

After listening for five minutes, Jiang Nian's inner monologue went like this:

( ´ ▽ ` ), as expected of a perfect-score student, she's really got something. Mm, I get it!

Ten minutes:

( _ ), she seems to be really enjoying her explanation. Should I interrupt her?

Twenty minutes:

(﹃), Master, please stop chanting. I want to die!

Half an hour:

(╯▔皿▔)╯She's even more of a nag than my mom!

"So, did you remember everything I just said?" Xu Qianqian's mouth was dry from talking. She took a sip of the now-cold soy milk, having taught him all her life's secrets.

"I remember, but not completely." Jiang Nian instantly stood up and walked right out. "Wait for me to mull it over. I'll talk to you again this afternoon."

"Hey! You..." Xu Qianqian watched his retreating back, wanting to grind her teeth to bits.

This guy really wasted half an hour of her time!

Back home, Jiang Nian opened the panel.

[Quest: Have a pleasant conversation with Xu Qianqian. (Complete)

Reward: Memory Bread (five hours). In this state, you can quickly memorize knowledge.]

After listening to a half-hour learning seminar, he had finally obtained the quest reward. Almost instantly, a piece of bread the size of a Daliyuan pastry appeared in his hand.

Nice, real-time settlement.

Jiang Nian rubbed his chin. He was a practical person. Xu Qianqian was right, he couldn't just keep slacking off. The most important thing right now was still the gaokao.

Personally, as a resident of a small county town, Jiang Nian's starting point was a notch higher than that of kids from the countryside. At least he had a safety net; if school didn't work out, he could come back and find a job through connections.

But, that wasn't what he wanted.

Studying was still the best way for an ordinary person to change their fate!

Besides, getting into a good university not only meant lower tuition fees, but it would also allow his parents to hold their heads a little higher.

Rote memorization wouldn't get you a high score, but your score definitely wouldn't be low. If he had five hours of memory time, it would be more than enough to browse through the 3,500-word gaokao vocabulary.

But using it all to memorize vocabulary would be a bit of a waste. In reality, you only needed to master seventy to eighty percent of the words for your English score not to be too bad.

So the time had to be allocated rationally, as other subjects also had key points that needed memorizing.

Jiang Nian flipped to the first page and was immediately at a loss for words.

"abandon"

(End of this chapter)
